name: blast-unevacuated-casualties
description: The punishment path for issue #557: drill, charge and sequence a pattern, then fire WITHOUT ever running `zone clear` — the staffed driller/blaster crew and the drill_rig they drove out on are left standing exactly where their own work left them. Deterministic on seed 42: the crew dies, one vehicle is destroyed, and the incident record shows it. This is the cost the tutorial's evacuate-zone step (and blastCommand's tutorial-mode refusal) exist to prevent.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:8 diameter:0.089 start:15,15
steps.description: 3x3 grid at the grid tool's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3) — the (15,15)-(21,21) drag needs no spacing-stepper click first. #947 CI-fix: `diameter:0.089` added to match Drill.ts's DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M — the grid tool has no diameter stepper, so interaction mode always confirms at the UI's fixed 89mm regardless of clicks, while this command previously fell back to drillPlan.ts's own 0.15 default; that gap fed computeDrillHoleDurationTicks a different diameter per mode (same class of bug as blast-charge-loading-ui.json's #947 fix). Depth also diverged: the grid tool's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M is 6m, not this command's declared 8m, and nothing below clicked the depth stepper to raise it — so interaction mode drilled shallower/faster holes than command mode simulated. Two increment clicks on the depth stepper (data-field="depth", default 6 -> 8) raise interaction mode's grid depth to match the command's own explicit depth:8 before the drag+confirm, instead of watering the scenario's declared depth down to the UI default.
#553/#590: drain the ordered drill plan — sandbox-measured landing well inside 300 ticks for the staffed roster's lone driller/drill_rig on this 9-hole grid.
Deliberately under-stemmed (0.5m on 8m holes) — the reckless overcharge this file is built around, matching the flyrock-danger integration suite's own reckless config.
#554: drain the charge order(s) — sandbox-measured landing well inside 200 ticks.

The blast panel is already open (opened once in the drill_plan step and never closed) and, by the time the preceding charge order has drained, BlastWorkshop's own autoAdvance/suggestStep has already moved it to the Sequence tab on its own. A bare clickSelector on the toolbar's blast tab here would hit togglePanel's already-open branch and close the panel instead of a no-op, leaving the very next click on a hidden, zero-size auto-sequence button (UIManager.togglePanel, src/ui/UIManager.ts) — ensurePanel is idempotent and only clicks when the panel isn't already open.

No `zone clear` anywhere in this file — the crew that drilled and charged this pattern is left standing exactly where its own work left it, and so is the drill_rig it drove out on. This is what the evacuate-zone tutorial step and blastCommand's tutorial-mode refusal exist to prevent (#557).

expect.note: Deterministic on seed 42: the driller and blaster who charged this pattern die where they stood; the drill_rig they drove out on (and a second vehicle) is destroyed too. #947 CI-fix: deathCount re-pinned 3 -> 2. The drill_plan step's own diameter/depth parity fix (above) changes how many ticks drilling+charging take before this step's own fire, which shifts this seed's RNG draw sequence downstream (fragment ejection is randomized per fragment, not positional-only) enough that the bystander driver #928 pinned as a third casualty (Pete Crater, ~17m from the nearest hole) is no longer in a projectile's path — confirmed identical (deathCount 2, driller+blaster only, Pete Crater alive) in both command mode and a real interaction-mode run once drilling/charging simulate the same diameter and depth in both channels; previously interaction mode silently drilled shallower (6m not 8m) and narrower (89mm UI default vs the command's unstated 150mm fallback) holes than command mode simulated, so the two channels' own pre-#947 pinned value was never actually reproduced by a real browser session, only by command mode's own now-corrected timing. Nobody was evacuated — that's the whole point of this file.
